decision_log.decision: Organise the 7.20 x 4.50 room as two zones side by side on the long axis (living west, dining east) with a thick brick hearth core projecting from the internal north wall at their junction, and gather all service functions (entry door, coats cupboard, hearth, sideboard, kitchen door) in a strip along that north wall.
decision_log.rationale: The core marks the junction and both zones flow past it on the room side; the north strip keeps the principal space along the glazed south wall uninterrupted, reading long and low.

decision_log.decision: Entry by a plain flush oak door at the west end of the north wall into a 1.20 m deep gallery under a 2.10 m soffit, beside the full-height coats cupboard and the chimney mass, from which the room opens south and east; no surround, not on any axis with the hearth or windows.
decision_log.rationale: A compressed vestibule beside a solid mass is the prescribed entry sequence; placing door, hearth and window groups on different centrelines keeps the composition asymmetric.

decision_log.decision: Provide the brief's ceiling change as two dropped plaster soffits at 2.10 m within a flat 2.40 m ceiling: the entry gallery soffit (x 0.00-2.10, y 3.30-4.50) and a 0.35 m eave soffit over the south glazed band (x 0.00-7.20, y 0.00-0.35), each with a cast-stone fascia band; no level change.
decision_log.rationale: The ceiling edge becomes a deep horizontal band oversailing the glazing heads, the gallery soffit makes the low entry, and the ceiling stays flat; a floor step would steal height from a 2.40 m room.

decision_log.decision: Define the two zones without a wall: the hearth core and its plinth blocks (x 1.80-3.90, projecting 0.90 m from the north wall), the gallery soffit, the rug and the furniture groups mark the junction; no partition element spans the room width.
decision_log.rationale: The designer's core sits between the two rooms with passage past it so they read as one space; nothing here closes the width.

decision_log.decision: South wall as a continuous band of five 0.84 m floor-to-head glazed bays between 0.38 m brick piers on a 1.22 m module, stopping one pier short of the corners with unequal corner piers (0.55 m west, 0.93 m east); bays S03 and S05 are outward-swinging terrace leaves, S01, S02 and S04 fixed lights.
decision_log.rationale: The long outer wall is a glazed band of narrow leaves between short piers, head at the ceiling band, opening outward; the unequal corner piers absorb the module remainder and keep the band off the room centreline.

decision_log.decision: End walls each as a full-width group of three 0.84 m lights between brick piers (corner piers 0.46 m south, 0.76 m north) on a 0.90 m cast-stone sill course over a brick spandrel, each light a pair of 0.40 m tall narrow casements with a leaded straight-line ladder lattice; a built-in zinc-lined oak planter trough sits on the east sill.
decision_log.rationale: A plain rectangular room gets no prow bay; the end wall is expressed as a window group between piers on the same module, with the lattice where glass is detailed and planting built in on the sill rather than in pots.

decision_log.decision: Fireplace as a plain brick breast 1.50 m wide projecting 0.90 m, rising to the ceiling and capped by the cast-stone head band, with a 0.90 x 0.55 m fire opening raised 0.40 m, three 0.12 m square recesses, no mantel, and cast-stone plinth blocks stepping out 0.30 m on both sides.
decision_log.rationale: The hearth is a masonry core on the internal wall, not a surround on an exterior wall; the chimney breast is a plain capped brick slab with small recesses; plinths step out at both sides and every masonry edge gets a light cap.

decision_log.decision: Seat eight at a 2.60 x 1.00 m oak slab table along the long axis (x 3.90-6.50, y 1.20-2.20), four tall-backed oak chairs a side and no end chairs; 0.70 m from the east wall, 0.70 m behind the south chairs to the glazing, 1.35 m behind the north chairs to the sideboard.
decision_log.rationale: End chairs would need 1.20 m more length than the room allows; a 4+4 table keeps the dining group reading as one long low slab parallel to the datum bands and clears the promenade.

decision_log.decision: Living group: three-seat sofa facing north toward the fire across the promenade (x 1.00-3.00), armchair beside a built-in cast-stone window seat under the west windows, oak slab low table at the 0.40 m plinth datum, flatweave rug stopping at the promenade edge.
decision_log.rationale: The passage past the core is the designer's own move, so the group faces the hearth across it; the window seat is a plinth slab under the sill course with the brick spandrel as its back.

decision_log.decision: Built-ins and joinery (coats cupboard, sideboard, table, chairs, low table, pendant housing) built from stacked oak slabs and square posts with square pulls on a grid; sideboard capped by a cast-stone slab at 0.90 m continuous with the sill-course datum; no curved profile anywhere.
decision_log.rationale: Profiles are stacked rectangular layers, never carved or turned; the cap on a built-in is a plain light band; the shared 0.90 m datum runs the room long and low.

decision_log.decision: Materials and palette: tawny brick in horizontal coursing against pale cast-stone bands, oiled oak joinery, warm white limewashed plaster, oxblood leather and oatmeal textured wool as accents, patinated bronze hardware; no mirrored panels, no gloss on any wall.
decision_log.rationale: Dark brick bands between light horizontal strips, with oak, leather and stippled upholstery as the warm accents, is the designer's stated material language and meets the brief's material bans.

decision_log.decision: Floor finish: wide-board European oak, 180 mm boards, matt hardwax oil, laid east-west along the long axis in both zones.
decision_log.rationale: A single light warm floor keeps the low room bright and the boards running the long way reinforce the horizontal reading.

decision_log.decision: Proportions held to four horizontal datums (0.40 plinth, 0.90 sill course, 2.10 head band, 2.40 ceiling); fire opening and shelf slabs markedly wider than high; dining chair backs tall and narrow (1.15 m high on a 0.42 m width); living seating low and wide.
decision_log.rationale: Continuous sill and head bands make the room read long and low, and the designer's openings are wider than high while the dining chairs are tall-backed and the living chairs shorter and wider.

decision_log.decision: Lighting: linear oak-and-bronze pendant slab over the table, concealed strips in the ceiling steps and on top of the head band, two downlights grazing the breast, table lamps on the sideboard, low-glare downlights in the gallery soffit.
decision_log.rationale: Light is laid in continuous horizontal lines along the bands and soffit steps, and the fittings are stacked slabs and blocks.

decision_log.decision: Circulation: a straight promenade along y 3.15 from the west wall to the east wall, clear between y 2.70 and y 3.60 (0.90 m minimum, 1.00 m actual), passing the hearth core and the north side of the table; a secondary route along the glazed band and through the 1.00 m gap between sofa and dining chairs.
decision_log.rationale: The two zones flow past the core along one line; the route also links entry, terrace leaves and kitchen door.

decision_log.decision: Hinge and swing choices: entry door hinged west, swinging in across x 0.15-1.05 / y 3.60-4.50 with nothing inside the arc; kitchen door and terrace leaves swing out.
decision_log.rationale: Keeps every swing clear of furniture and the promenade.

conflicts.constraint: Brief names the fireplace / hearth WALL as the principal elevation and requires a 0.90 m clear path end to end in a 7.20 x 4.50 m room.
conflicts.resolution: A freestanding core on the long axis with passage on both sides would leave no hearth wall to draw and would block the dining group, so the hearth is built as a thick brick core projecting 0.90 m from the internal north wall at the zone junction, with the fire opening facing the room and passage past it on the room side only. Brief favoured on buildability; the rule is kept in its internal-wall, masonry-mass form.

conflicts.constraint: Stated room dimensions 7.20 x 4.50 m are not multiples of the 1.22 m pier module.
conflicts.resolution: Module kept at 0.84 m light + 0.38 m pier; the remainder is taken up in unequal corner piers (0.55 / 0.93 m on the south wall, 0.46 / 0.76 m on the end walls). Brief dimensions untouched.

conflicts.constraint: Brief room is a plain rectangle; no bay is allowed.
conflicts.resolution: No prow bay faked; both end walls expressed as full-width window groups between piers, as the rule's own fallback.

conflicts.constraint: Brief requires an 8-seat dining group inside the room with no furniture in door swings; chairs sit 0.70 m from the south band.
conflicts.resolution: The three bays behind sofa and dining table (S01, S02, S04) are fixed lights rather than opening leaves; the two leaves that open (S03, S05) face clear floor. The band stays continuous floor to head.
